questions.question: P, Q and R invested Rs. 7200, 8400 and 9600 respectively. If the ratio of their profit earned is 3 ∶ 7 ∶ 16. Find the ratio of the time for which they invested their capitals?
questions.explanation:
The ratio of their profit earned = 3 ∶ 7 ∶ 16     ----(1)

Let the time for which P invested its capital = x years

The time for which Q invested its capital = y years

The time for which R invested its capital = Z years

P’s profit  = 7200 × x

Q’s profit = 8400 × y

R’s profit = 9600 × z

Ratio of profits = 7200x : 8400y : 9600z

⇒  6x ∶ 7y ∶ 8z         ---(2)

Comparing equation (1) and equation (2),

6x ∶ 7y = 3 : 7

⇒ 6x/7y = 3/7

⇒ x/y = 3/7 × 7/6 = 1/2

So, x : y = 1 : 2

7y ∶ 8z = 7 : 16

⇒ 7y/8z = 7/16

⇒ y/z = 7/16 × 8/7 = 1/2

So, y : z = 1 : 2

Multiply numerator and numerator  by 2,

y : z = (2 × 1) : (2 × 2) = 2 : 4

So, x : y : z = 1: 2 : 4

∴ The ratio of times for which they invested their capital is 1 : 2 : 4.

questions.question: X and Y invest in a company in the ratio 2: 3. If 10% of the total profit goes to charity and Y's share is Rs. 600, the total profit is:
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Investment ratio of X : Y = 2 : 3
  • 10% of total profit is given to charity
  • Y’s share = Rs. 600

Calculation:

Let total profit = 100

10% goes to charity → remaining = 90

X : Y = 2 : 3
Total parts = 5

Y’s share = (3/5) × 90 = 54

So when total profit = 100, Y gets 54

But actually Y gets 600

54 → 600
100 → ?

Total profit = (600 × 100) / 54
= 1111.11

Final Answer: ₹1111.11 (approx.)

Used Concept:

After deducting charity, remaining profit is divided in the ratio of their investments.

questions.question: There is a partnership of 3 people in a company. They shared the profit in this company in the ratio 3 : 5 : 6. They had invested for 10 months, 6 months and 5 months respectively. What was the ratio of their investments?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Profit ratio of three partners = 3 : 5 : 6
• Time period of investment = 10 months, 6 months, and 5 months respectively

Calculation:
Investment ratio = Profit ratio / Time period ratio
Investment ratio = (3 / 10) : (5 / 6) : (6 / 5)
LCM of denominators (10, 6, and 5) = 30
Multiplying each term by 30:
Investment ratio = (3 / 10) × 30 : (5 / 6) × 30 : (6 / 5) × 30
Investment ratio = 9 : 25 : 36

Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.question: A and B start a business and invest Rs 50,000 and Rs 70,000 respectively. B is an active partner and she gets 10% of the profit separately. If their business yields them a total of Rs 80,000 as profit, what is the share of B at the end of a year?

A share is Rs. 50000

B share is Rs. 70000

Ratio of their share is 50000:70000

Is 5:7

Total profit is Rs.80,000

B is an active partner and she gets 10% of the profit separately

So 10% of 80000 is

\(\frac{10}{100} \times 80000 = 8000\)

After 10% by B as an active partner remaining profit is 90%

90% of 80000 is

\(\frac{90}{100} \times 80000 = 72000\)

B share is \(= \frac{\text{B ratio}}{\text{Sum of  all ratios}} \times \text{Total  Profit}\)

\(= \frac{7}{12} \times 72000\)

\(= 42000\)

questions.question: Ajay and Vijay started a business by investing in a ratio 5:9. Ajay insvested the amount for the whole year while Vijay invested the amount for half year. Find the ratio in which profit is divided between them?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Ajay and Vijay invested their capitals in the ratio 5 : 9
• Ajay invested his money for the whole year, that is 12 months
• Vijay invested his money for half year, that is 6 months

Calculation:

Let the investments of Ajay and Vijay be 5x and 9x respectively.

Ajay invested for 12 months, so his capital–time = 5x × 12 = 60x.
Vijay invested for 6 months, so his capital–time = 9x × 6 = 54x.

Now, the ratio of profit between Ajay and Vijay is
60x : 54x = 10 : 9.

Therefore, the profit is divided between Ajay and Vijay in the ratio 10 : 9.

Hence, option C is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Profit ratio = Capital × Time

questions.question: Mohan and Nilesh entered into a partnership with capitals in the ratio 8 : 7. After 5 months, Mohan withdrew \(\frac{1}{4}\) of its capital and Nilesh withdrew 17 of its capital. The gain at the end of the year was Rs. 4770. Mohan’s share in this profit is:

• After 5 months withdrawal: Mohan 1 ÷ 4, Nilesh 1 ÷ 7
• Total time = 12 months
• Profit = 4770

Mohan:
First 5 months = 8 × 5 = 40
Remaining = 8 × 3 ÷ 4 = 6
Next 7 months = 6 × 7 = 42
Total = 82

Nilesh:
First 5 months = 7 × 5 = 35
Remaining = 7 × 6 ÷ 7 = 6
Next 7 months = 6 × 7 = 42
Total = 77

Ratio = 82 : 77

Mohan’s share = 4770 × 82 ÷ (82 + 77)
= 4770 × 82 ÷ 159
= 2460

Hence, option (C) is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Profit ∝ Capital × Time
• Withdrawal adjustment
• Ratio distribution

questions.question: Harsh and Vikas entered into a partnership and invested Rs. 3000 and Rs. 5000 respectively. If they split one fifth of the profit equally for their efforts and the balance in the ratio of their investments, then Vikas got Rs. 600 more than Harsh. Find the profit gained by the them?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Harsh invested Rs. 3,000, Vikas invested Rs. 5,000
• 1/5 of total profit is split equally for their efforts
• Remaining profit is divided in the ratio of their investments
• Vikas received Rs. 600 more than Harsh

Calculation:

Investment of Harsh is Rs. 3000

Investment of Vikas is Rs. 5000

Ratio of their investment 3:5

\(\frac{1}{5}\) of the profit is distributed equally between them

Let total profit be 5x

And x be distributed equally between them

So they both get \(\frac{x}{2}\) each

Remaining profit of 4x is distributed according to ratio of their investment

Harsh get \(= \frac{\text{Harsh ratio}}{\text{Sum of  all  ratios}} \times \text{Total Profit}\)

\(= \frac{3}{8} \times 4x\)

\(= 1.5x\)

Vikas get \(= \frac{\text{Vikas ratio}}{\text{Sum of  all  ratios}} \times \text{Total  Profit}\)

\(= \frac{5}{8} \times 4x\)

\(= 2.5x\)

Total profit of Harsh is \(0.5x + 1.5x = 2x\)

Total profit of Vikas is \(0.5x + 2.5x = 3x\)

Vikas got Rs. 600 more than Harsh

\(3x - 2x = 600\)

\(x = 600\)

Total profit is 5x\(= 5 \times 600\)

Total profit is Rs. 3000

Hence, option D is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Total profit = P
• Effort share = 1/5 of total profit, divided equally
• Investment share = remaining 4/5 of profit, divided in ratio of investments
• Individual profit = Effort share + Investment share

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following question carefully and choose the right answer given beside.

Three persons Alpesh, Mukesh and Rakesh invested different amounts in a fixed deposit scheme for one year at the rate of 12% per annum and earned a total interest of Rs 3240 at the end of the year. If the amount invested by Mukesh is Rs 5000 more than the amount invested by Alpesh and the invested by Rakesh is Rs 2000 more than the amount invested by Mukesh, what is the amount invested by Mukesh?
questions.explanation:
From the given information,

Let the amount invested by Alpesh be a

Amount invested by Mukesh = a + 5000

Amount invested by Rakesh = a + 7000

Now, According to the question,

Rate = 12%, Total Interest = Rs 3240

\(\Rightarrow \{ a + (a + 5000) + (a + 7000)\} \times \frac{12}{100} = 3240\)

\(\Rightarrow 3a + 12000 = \frac{324000}{12}\)

⇒ 3a = 15000 ⇒ a = 5000

Therefore, amount invested by Mukesh = 5000 + 5000 = Rs 10000

questions.question: Amit and Sumit enter into a partnership for a year. Amit invests Rs. 3000, and Sumit invests Rs. 5000. After 6 months, they admit Nain, who invests Rs. 12000. If Sumit withdraws his contribution after 6 months, how would Amit’s share in a profit of Rs 4600 at the end of the year?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Amit invested Rs. 3,000 for the full year
• Sumit invested Rs. 5,000 but withdrew after 6 months
• Nain joined after 6 months with Rs. 12,000
• Total duration = 12 months
• Total profit = Rs. 4,600

Calculation:

Amount invest by Amit (C1) is 3000

Amount invest by Sumit (C2) is 5000

Amount invest by Nain is (C3) 12000

Amit’s time (T1) be 12 months

Sumit’s time (T2) be 6 months

Nain’s time (T3) be 6 months

Profit to be divided is 4600

Profit divided in the ratio:\((C1 \times T1:C2 \times T2:C3 \times T3)\)

\(3000 \times 12:5000 \times 6:12000 \times 6\)

6:5:12

Sum of ratios is 23

Amit’s shares \(= \frac{Amit's\ ratio}{\text{Sum of  all  ratios}} \times \text{Total  Profit}\)

\(= \frac{6}{23} \times 4600\)

\(= 1200\)

Amit’s share is Rs.1200
Hence, option B is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Profit ratio = Capital × Time
• Individual profit share = (Capital–time ÷ Total capital–time) × Total profit

questions.question: Suman being a working partner gets x% of the profit as salary, the remaining is shared between Suman, Sneha and Samantha in the ratio 3 : 7 : 11. If Suman gets Rs. 4000 out of total profit of Rs 14,000, then find the salary (in Rs.) of Suman?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Total profit = Rs. 14,000
• Suman gets x% of profit as salary
• Remaining profit is shared among Suman, Sneha and Samantha in the ratio 3 : 7 : 11
• Total profit received by Suman = Rs. 4,000

Calculation:

Let Suman’s salary be Rs. S.
Then remaining profit after salary = 14,000 − S.

The ratio of Suman : Sneha : Samantha is 3 : 7 : 11, so total parts = 21.

Suman’s share from the remaining profit
= (3 ÷ 21) × (14,000 − S)
= (1 ÷ 7) × (14,000 − S)
= 2000 − S/7.

Total amount received by Suman
= Salary + Share from remaining profit
= S + 2000 − S/7.

According to the question, this total is Rs. 4,000.
So,
S + 2000 − S/7 = 4000.

Multiplying the whole equation by 7,
7S + 14,000 − S = 28,000.

6S = 14,000.

S = 14,000 ÷ 6
S = 7,000 ÷ 3
S = Rs. 2333.33 (approx).

Therefore, the salary of Suman is Rs. 2333.33 (approximately).

Hence, option C is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Salary is deducted first from total profit
• Remaining profit is divided in the given ratio
• Individual share = (Individual ratio ÷ Total ratio) × Remaining profit

questions.question: 'A', 'B' and 'C' started a business by investing Rs. 3,600, Rs. 4,950 and Rs. 6,750, respectively. After 1 year, 'A', 'B' and 'C' increased their respective investments by 25%, Rs. 900 and 20%. If 2 years after starting the business, the profit share of 'B' is Rs. 2,000 more than that of 'A', then find the profit share of 'C'.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Initial investment of A = Rs. 3,600
• Initial investment of B = Rs. 4,950
• Initial investment of C = Rs. 6,750
• After 1 year, A increased his investment by 25%
• After 1 year, B increased his investment by Rs. 900
• After 1 year, C increased his investment by 20%
• Difference between profit shares of B and A after 2 years = Rs. 2,000

Calculation:
Investment of A for the second year = 3600 × 1.25 = Rs. 4,500
Investment of B for the second year = 4950 + 900 = Rs. 5,850
Investment of C for the second year = 6750 × 1.20 = Rs. 8,100
Since the time duration for each investment phase is 1 year:
Ratio of profit shares of A, B, and C = (3600 + 4500) : (4950 + 5850) : (6750 + 8100)
Ratio of profit shares of A, B, and C = 8100 : 10800 : 14850
Dividing each by 1350:
Ratio of profit shares of A, B, and C = 6 : 8 : 11
Let the profit shares of A, B, and C be 6x, 8x, and 11x, respectively.
Difference between profit shares of B and A = 8x - 6x = 2x
According to the question:
2x = 2000
x = 1000
Profit share of C = 11x = 11 × 1000 = Rs. 11,000

Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.question: Amit and Ragav enter a partnership by investing Rs.6000 and Rs.10000 respectively. After 'x' months, Amit added Rs.1000 to his investment. After next 'x' months, Ragav withdrew Rs.1000. At the end of year partnership, profit earned by Amit and Ragav is in the ratio 5: 7 respectively. What is the value of 'x'?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Amit invested Rs. 6,000 initially
• Ragav invested Rs. 10,000 initially
• After 'x' months, Amit added Rs. 1,000
• After next 'x' months, Ragav withdrew Rs. 1,000
• Total duration of business = 12 months
• Profit ratio of Amit : Ragav = 5 : 7

Calculation:

Amount invested by Amit \(=\) 6000

Amount invested by Ragav \(=\) 10000

Amount invested by Amit after x months is 7000

Amount invested by Ragav after withdrawal of Rs. 1000 is \(=\) 9000

Total Amount invested by Amit \(= 6000 \times x + (12 - x)7000\)

Total Amount invested by Ragav \(= 10000 \times x\  + (12 - x)9000\)

Ratio of profit distributed by them is 5:7

Apply formula: \(\frac{C1\  \times \ T1}{C2\  \times \ T2} = \frac{P1}{P2}\ \)

\(\frac{6000 \times x + (12 - x)7000}{10000 \times x + (12 - x)9000}\  = \ \left( \frac{5}{7} \right)\)

\(\frac{6x + (12 - x)7}{10x + (12 - x)9}\  = \ \left( \frac{5}{7} \right)\)

\(42x + 588 - 49x = 50x + 540 - 45x\)

\(48 = 12x\)

\(4 = x\)
Hence, option D is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Profit ratio = Capital × Time
• If capital changes, divide the time periods accordingly and compute capital–time for each period

questions.question: Sum of the amount invested by Kunal and Gourav is Rs.10000. Kunal invested 10% more than Akshay who invested Rs.5000 and joined Kunal and Gourav after 7 months. Gourav investment is \((10000 - 5500) = 4500\)

Time spent by Kunal is 12 months

Time spent by Gourav is 9 months

Time spent by Akshay is 5 months

\(5500 \times 12\ :\ 4500 \times 9\ :\ 5000 \times 5\)

132 : 81 : 50

Akshay’s shares \(= \frac{Akshay's\ ratio}{\text{Sum of all ratios}} \times \text{Total  Profit}\)

\(= \frac{50}{263} \times 7890\)

\(= 1500\)

Akshay’s share is Rs.1500

Hence, option E is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Profit ratio = Capital × Time
• Individual profit share = (Capital–time ÷ Total capital–time) × Total profit

questions.question:
Persons P and Q started the business and after 3 months P added ₹2000 more to his capital while Q withdraws ₹2000 from his capital. If the ratio of their initial investment is 5: 7 and the ratio of their profit share at the end of 8 months is 15: 17, find the ratio of their profit share at the end of a year.

Assume investment remains unchanged after 3 months.

Let initial capital of P and Q is 5x and 7x respectively.

Ratio of profit share of P to Q = [5x × 3 + (5x + 2000) × 5]: [7x × 3 + (7x - 2000) × 5] = 15: 17

[40x + 10000]: [56x - 10000] = 15: 17

680x + 170000 = 840x - 150000

160x = 320000

x = 2000

questions.question: P and Q enter into a partnership and invested Rs. 42000 and Rs. 54000 respectively. If they split half of the profit equally for their efforts and the remaining balance in the ratio of their investments, then Q got Rs. 510 more than P. What was the profit made in the partnership ?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • P invested ₹42,000 and Q invested ₹54,000.
  • Half of the total profit is shared equally for their efforts.
  • The remaining half is shared in the ratio of their investments (42,000 : 54,000 = 7 : 9).
  • Q received ₹510 more than P.

Calculation:

The ratio of investment of P and Q is 42000: 54000 = 7: 9

Let total profit = X

Using the data provided in the question, we get

Difference between Q and P’s profit =916×X2-7X16 × 2=510

2X = 510 × 16 × 2

X = Rs. 8160

Concept Used:
When profit is distributed partly equally and partly in the ratio of investments, the extra amount received by one partner comes only from the ratio-based portion, and that difference helps to find the total profit.

questions.question: A and B enter into a partnership with their capital of ₹7000 and ₹8400 respectively. They invested for 15 months and 10 months respectively and out of total profit from the business, 28% is divided between them equal and remaining according to their investment. Find the final ratio of profit shares of A to B.
questions.explanation:
Ratio of profit share of A to B = [7000 × 15]: [8400 × 10] = 105000: 84000 = 5: 4

Let total profit = 100x

Remaining profit = 100x - 28% of 100x = 72x

Profit share of A = 40x + 14x = 54x

Profit share of B = 32x + 14x = 46x

Required ratio = 54x: 46x

= 27: 23

questions.question: A and B start a coffee shop with an investment of Rs 15000 and Rs 8000 respectively. If A is a working partner and takes 25% of the total profit as his salary and remaining profit is divided according to their investment. In this process A receives Rs 44000 more than B as a profit. calculate the overall profit?
questions.explanation:
Let overall profit be 92x.

Ratio of their profit\(\  = \ 15000:8000 = 15:8\)

Amount received by A as salary\(= 25\%\ of\ 92x\  = \ 23x\)

Remaining profit\(\ \  = \ 92x - 23x\  = \ 69x\)

A/Q;

A’s share of profit \(= \ \frac{15}{23} \times \ 69x\  = \ 45x\)

& B’s share\(\  = \ \frac{8}{23} \times 69\  = \ 24x\)

Amount received by A = 44000 +Amount received by B

\(= > \ 45x + 23x\  = \ 44000 + \ 24x\)

\(= > \ 68x\  = \ 44000 + 24x\)

\(= > \ 44x\  = \ 44000\)

\(= > \ x = 1000\)

Overall profit\(= \ 92x = \ 92 \times 1000 = \ 92000\)

questions.question: Arun, Varun and Tarun started a business by investing amounts in the ratio of 8 : 6 : 15. After one year, they earned a total profit of Rs 12000; out of which Arun’s profit share was Rs 4000 which was Rs 1000 more than Varun’s profit share. Find the respective ratio of the time for which they had invested the amounts?
questions.explanation:
Arun’s profit share = Rs 4000

Varun’s profit share = 4000 – 1000 = Rs 3000

Tarun’s share =  12000 – (4000 + 3000) = Rs 5000

Ratio of profits of Arun, Varun and Tarun = 4000 : 3000 : 5000 = 4 : 3 : 5

So, total investments of Arun, Varun and Tarun are in the ratio of 4 : 3 : 5

Let Arun, Varun and Tarun invested Rs 8x, 6x and 15x respectively and their time of investment was T1, T2 and T3 months respectively.

8x × T1 : 6x × T2 : 15x × T3 = 4 : 3 : 5

8T1 : 6T2 = 4 : 3

T1 :  T2 = 1 : 1

6T2 : 15T3 = 3 : 5

T2 : T3 = 3 : 2

Required ratio =  3 : 3 : 2

Option ‘3 : 3 : 2’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Arvind, Balkrishna and Chandrabhan started a business by investing amounts in the ratio of 5: 3: 4. After 8 months, Arvind invested the same amount as he invested before and Balkrishna withdrew 1/6 amount while Chandrabhan withdrew half of his investment. If at the end of a year, Chandrbhan earned a profit of Rs 3300, then find the difference between the profits earned by Arvind and Balkrishna.
questions.explanation:
Let the initial investments of Arvind, Balkrishna and Chandrabhan be Rs 5x, 3x and 4x respectively.

According to the question,

Arvind’s investment : Balkrishna’s investment : Chandrabhan’s investment for a year

= (5x × 8+10x× 4) : (3x× 8+(5x/2) × 4) : (4x × 8+2x× 4)

= 80x : 34x : 40x = 40 : 17 : 20

Difference between the profits earned by Arvind and Balkrishna

=  40- 1720 × 3300

= Rs 3795

Option ‘3795’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Mayank started a business which was joined by Sudeep after 3 months such that the capital of Sudeep is ₹5000 more than that of Mayank. If Mayank adds ₹10000 more to his capital after 3 months from the start of the business and his share from annual profit is ₹11340 out of total profit of ₹19440, find the sum of initial capital of both the persons together.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Total annual profit = ₹19,440
• Mayank's share in profit = ₹11,340
• Sudeep joined after 3 months with capital ₹5,000 more than Mayank's initial capital
• Mayank added ₹10,000 to his capital after 3 months

Calculation:
Let Mayank's initial capital be ₹x.
Sudeep's initial capital = ₹(x + 5000)
Sudeep's share in profit = ₹19440 - ₹11340 = ₹8100
Ratio of profit share of Mayank to Sudeep = 11340 : 8100 = 7 : 5
Mayank's total investment = (x × 3) + (x + 10000) × 9 = 12x + 90000
Sudeep's total investment = (x + 5000) × 9 = 9x + 45000
(12x + 90000) / (9x + 45000) = 7 / 5
5 × (12x + 90000) = 7 × (9x + 45000)
60x + 450000 = 63x + 315000
3x = 135000
x = 45000
Initial capital of Mayank = ₹45000
Initial capital of Sudeep = 45000 + 5000 = ₹50000
Sum of initial capital of both persons = 45000 + 50000 = ₹95000

Hence, option (E) is correct.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following question carefully and choose the right answer given beside.

Ramesh starts a business with Rs. 3900. After 3 months, Shankar joins as a partner with a capital of Rs. 5200 again after some months Mohit joins as a partner with a capital of Rs. 6500. The total profit of one year is Rs.2900 but Mohit already has withdrawn Rs. 100 per month from his profit so the remaining profit was divided in the ratio of 6: 6: 1 respectively. Find for how many months does Mohit join?
questions.explanation:
From the given information,

The ratio of Ramesh’s: Shankar’s: Mohit’s share

= 3900 × 12 : 5200 × 9 : a × 6500 (assume Mohit joins for a months) = 36 : 36 : 5a ......... (1)

The total money, Mohit has withdrawn from his profit in a months = 100 × a = 100a

Remaining = 2900 – 100a, it was divided in the ratio of 6 : 6 : 1 respectively.

So Ramesh’s share \(= \frac{6}{13} \times (2900 - 100a) =\) Shankar’s share

Mohit’s share \(= \frac{1}{13} \times (2900 - 100a)\)

If Mohit had not withdraw Rs. 100 per month then his profit would have been,

\(= \frac{1}{13} \times (2900 - 100a) + 100a\)

From the equation (i) , Rammesh’s share: Mohit’s share

\(\Rightarrow \frac{36}{5a} = \frac{\frac{6}{13} \times (2900 - 100a)}{\frac{1}{13} \times (2900 - 100a) + 100a}\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{36}{5a} = \frac{6 \times (2900 - 100a)}{2900 - 100a + 1300a}\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{36}{5a} = \frac{6 \times (2900 - 100a)}{2900 + 1200a}\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{36}{5a} = \frac{6 \times (29 - a)}{29 + 12a}\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{36 \times (29 + 12a)}{5a} = 174 - 6a\)

\(\Rightarrow 1044 + 432a = 870a - 30a^{2}\)

\(\Rightarrow 30a^{2} - 438a + 1044 = 0\)

\(\Rightarrow 5a^{2} - 73a + 174 = 0\)

\(\Rightarrow a = \frac{73 \pm 43}{10}\)

\(\Rightarrow a = \frac{73 + 43}{10}\text{ or }\frac{73 - 43}{10}\)

\(\Rightarrow a = 11.6\ or\ 3\)

Therefore, Mohit joins for 11.6 months or 3 months.

questions.question:
'A', 'B' and 'C' started a business where 'B' invested Rs. 2,000 more than 'A' while 'C' invested Rs. 500 less than 75% of the amount invested by 'B'. 'C' invested for 4 months more than the time for which 'A' invested his capital while the time period for which 'B' invested was 10% less than the time for which 'A' invested. The profit share of 'B' was 65% more than that of 'A'.

Which among the following can be determined based on the above information?

I. The time period for which 'A' invested

II. Ratio of profit shares of 'B' and 'C' respectively

III. Average investment of 'A' and 'B' together.
questions.explanation:
Let the investment of 'A' = Rs. 'x'

Then investment of 'B' = Rs. (x + 2000)

Investment of 'C' = (x + 2000) × 0.75 - 500 = 0.75x + 1500 - 500 = Rs. (0.75x + 1000)

Let the time period for which 'A' invested be '10y' months

Then time period for which 'C' invested = (10y + 4) months

Time period for which 'B' invested = 10y × 0.9 = '9y' months

Ratio of profit shares of 'A' and B' respectively = (x × 10y):{(x + 2000) ×9y}

= 10xy:(9xy + 18000y)

According to the question,

10xy × 1.65 = 9xy + 18000y

Or, 16.5xy = 9xy + 18000y

Or, 7.5xy = 18000y

So, x = 18000 ÷ 7.5 = 2400

So, investments of 'A', 'B' and 'C' are Rs. 2,400, Rs. 4,400 and Rs. 2,800, respectively

So, ratio of profit shares of 'A' and 'B' = 24000y:39600y

We have, 39600y = 24000y × 1.65

So, the value of 'y' cannot be determined.

For I:

Since, the value of 'y' cannot be determined, the time period of investment of 'A' also cannot be determined.

So, statement I cannot be determined.

For II:

Ratio of profit shares of 'B' and 'C' respectively = (4400 × 9y):{2800 × (10y + 4)}

= 39600y:(28000y + 11200)

Since, the value of 'y' cannot be determined, the ratio of profit shares of 'B' and 'C' also cannot be determined.

So, statement II cannot be determined.

For III:

Average investment of 'A' and 'B' = (2400 + 4400) ÷ 2 = Rs. 3,400

So, statement III can be determined.

Hence, option A.

questions.question:
A and B started a business with initial investments of Rs. 2,400 and Rs. 2,500 respectively. After one year A withdrew ___% and B withdrew ____% of their initial investments. After two years profit share of A out of the total profit is more than 50%.

The values given in which of the following options will fill the blanks in the same order in which is it given to make the above statement true:

I. 20%, 30%

II. 25%, 30%

III. 12%, 16%
questions.explanation:
statement I:

Investment of A for second year = 2400 × 0.80 = Rs. 1,920

Investment of B for second share = 2500 × 0.70 = Rs. 1750

Ratio the profits of A to B = 2400 + 1920: 2500 + 1750 = 4320: 4250 = 432: 425

So the profit percent of A out of the total profit = 432\(\div\)(432 + 425) × 100 = 43200\(\div\)857 = 50.4%

So option I can be the answer.

statement II:

Investment of A for second year = 2400 × 0.75 = Rs. 1,800

Investment of B for second share = 2500 × 0.70 = Rs. 1750

Ratio the profits of A to B = 2400 + 1800: 2500 + 1750 = 4200: 4250 = 84: 85

So the profit percent of A out of the total profit = 84\(\div\)(84 + 85) × 100 = 8400\(\div\)169 = 49.7%

So option II can’t be the answer.

statement III:

Investment of A for second year = 2400 × 0.88 = Rs. 2,112

Investment of B for second share = 2500 × 0.84 = Rs. 2100

Ratio the profits of A to B = 2400 + 2112: 2500 + 2100 = 4512: 4600 = 564: 575

So the profit percent of A out of the total profit = 564\(\div\)(564 + 575) × 100 = 56400\(\div\)1139 = 49.51%

So option III can’t be the answer.

Hence, option b.

questions.question:
Ansu and Arya started a partnership business with total investment of Rs. 18000 and ratio of their investments was _______ respectively. After 8 months Arya left and Ansu increased his investment by 50%. If the total profit after a year is Rs.________, then Arya got Rs. 5000.

The values given in which of the following options will fill the blanks in the same order in which is it given to make the statement true:

I. 4:5, 12000

II. 1:2, 9375

III. 5:4, 9000
questions.explanation:
From I:

Ansu’s investment = 18000 × \(\frac{4}{9}\) = Rs. 8000

Arya’s investment = 18000 × \(\frac{5}{9}\) = Rs. 10000

Capital Ratio = {8000 × 8 + (8000 × 1.5) × 4}:(10000 × 8) = 7:5

Now, Arya got Rs. 5000

Now,

5 ratio → 5000

7 ratio → 7000

12 ratio → 12000

Hence, statement I holds.

From II:

Ansu;s investment = 18000 × \(\frac{1}{3}\) = Rs. 6000

Arya’s investment = 18000 × \(\frac{2}{3}\) = Rs. 12000

Capital Ratio = {6000 × 8 + (6000 × 1.5) × 4}:(12000 × 8) = 7:8

Now, Arya got Rs. 5000

Now,

8 ratio → 5000

15 ratio → (5000 × \(\frac{15}{8}\)) = 9375

Hence, statement II holds.

From III:

Ansu;s investment = 18000 × \(\frac{5}{9}\) = Rs. 10000

Arya’s investment = 18000 × \(\frac{4}{9}\) = Rs. 8000

Capital Ratio = {10000 × 8 + (10000 × 1.5) × 4}:(8000 × 8) = 35:16

Now, Arya got Rs. 5000

16 ratio → 5000

51 ratio → (5000 × \(\frac{51}{16}\)) = 15937.5

Hence, statement III does not hold.

Hence, option b.

questions.question:
M, N and O entered into a partnership. N invested Rs.1800 more than M and O invested Rs.900 more than M. After ‘T’ months, N withdrew his whole investment. At the end of the year, M invested his profit share in a scheme at 15% simple rate of interest for 2 years and O invested his profit share in another scheme at 5% simple rate of interest for 3 years. Interest received by M and O is Rs.5760 and Rs.4500 respectively?

Find that which of following can be determined?

B: Total profit received by them together.

C: Value of ‘T’.

And O’s investment = Rs. (x + 900)

Now,

Profit share of M = \(\frac{5760\  \times \ 100}{15\  \times \ 2} = \ Rs.19200\)

Profit share of O = \(\frac{4500\  \times \ 100}{\left( 5\  \times \ 3 \right)} = \ Rs.30000\)

Ratio of profit shares of M to O = 19200:30000 = 16:25

So,

\(\frac{x}{\left( x\  + \ 900 \right)} = \frac{16}{25}\)

25x = 16x + 14400

x = 1600

From A,

M’s investment = Rs.1600

N’s investment = 1600 + 1800 = Rs.3400

Required ratio = 1600:3400 = 8:17

From B,

Since, we don’t know the investment period of N, from which we cannot determine the profit-sharing ratio between of M, N and O.

So, total profit received by all the 3 persons together cannot be determined.

From C,

Value of ‘T’ cannot be determined.

Hence, only A can be determined.

questions.question:
Akash and Sunil entered into a business with initial investments of Rs. ‘A + 32’ and Rs. ‘A’ respectively. After ‘B’ months Viru joined them with an initial investment which was 20% more than that invested by Akash initially. At the end of ‘2B’ months ratio of profit share of Akash, Sunil and Viru was 6B:14C:9D respectively. Which of the following relation(s) is/are true?

I. D = 0.4B

II. A = 448C/[15D – 14C]

III. A = 224C/[3B – 7C]
questions.explanation:
Ratio of profit share of Akash, Sunil and Viru = [(A + 32) × 2B]:[A × 2B]:[1.2 × (A + 32) × B]

So, [(A + 32) × 2B]/[1.2 × (A + 32) × B] = 6B/9D

So, 2/1.2 = 2B/3D

So, D = 1.2B/3 = 0.4B

And, [A × 2B]:[1.2 × (A + 32) × B] = 14C/9D

So, A/[0.6 × (A + 32)] = 14C/9D

Or, A = 268.8C/[9D – 8.4C]

And, [(A + 32) × 2B]:[A × 2B] = 6B/14C = 3B/7C

Or, A = 224C/[3B – 7C]

Hence, option D.

questions.question: A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’ started a business by investing Rs. 800, Rs. 1,200 and Rs. 1,500, respectively. 6 months later, ‘A’ increased his investment by ‘y%’ while ‘B’ and ‘C’ decreased their investment by 25% and 40% such that at the end of first year, ratio of profit shares of ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’ was 6:7:8, respectively. = (800 × 6 + Y × 6):(1200 × 6 + 1200 × 0.75 × 6):(1500 × 6 + 1500 × 0.6 × 6) = 6:7:8

Or, (4800 + 6Y):(12600):(14400) = 6:7:8

Or, (4800 + 6Y) ÷ 6 = 12600 ÷ 7 = 1800

So, Y = 1000

So, ratio of profit shares of ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’ at the end of 2 years

= (800 × 6 + 1000 × 18):(1200 × 6 + 900 × 18):(1500 × 6 + 900 × 18)

= (22800):(23400):(25200) = 38:39:42

So, profit share of ‘B’ at the end of 2 years = 11900 ÷ (38 + 39 + 42) × 39 = Rs. 3,900

Hence, option d.

2Y – 8 + 112 – 4Y = 40 + 160 – 10Y

Hence answer is option D

questions.question:
P, Q & R started a business by investing of Rs. ( X+800), Rs.( X-600) & Rs. X for ‘ 5Y’ months, ‘ 4Y’ months and ‘ 4Y+1’ months respectively. Q received profit of Rs.325 out of total profit of Rs.1400. The present age of B is same as time period for which P has invested and present age of A is 60% more than that of B. If present age of C is 32.5% of present age of A, then age of A four years ago is equal to twice the present age of C.

If Z =\(\frac{X}{4\ Y}\), then find the value of Z.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Investments: P = Rs.(X + 800), Q = Rs.(X − 600), R = Rs.X

  • Time periods: P = 5Y months, Q = 4Y months, R = 4Y + 1 months

  • Total profit = Rs. 1,400

  • Q’s profit = Rs. 325

  • Age relations:

    • Present age of B = time period P invested

    • Present age of A = 60% more than B

    • Present age of C = 32.5% of present age of A

    • Age of A four years ago = twice present age of C

Calculation:

Present age of B = 5Y years

Present age of A = 5Y \(\times \frac{160}{100}\) = 8Y years

Present age of C = 8Y \(\times \frac{32.5}{100}\) = 3Y years

According to question,

8Y – 4 = 3Y \(\times\) 2

8Y – 6Y = 4

2Y = 4

Y = 2

Time period for which P,Q and R invested their investment

P invested for 10 months

Q invested for 8 months

R invested for 9 months

Profit sharing ratio of P,Q and R

= (X+800) \(\times\) 10 : (X – 600) \(\times\) 8 : X \(\times\) 9

According to question:

\(\frac{(X\  - \ 600) \times 8}{\left\lbrack \left( \left( X\  + \ 800 \right) \times 10 \right) + 9X \right\rbrack}\) = \(\frac{325}{1400\  - \ 325}\)

\(\frac{8X\  - \ 4800}{10X\  + \ 8000\  + \ 9X}\) = \(\frac{325}{1075}\)

\(\frac{8X\  - \ 4800}{10X\  + \ 8000\  + \ 9X}\) = \(\frac{13}{43}\)

344 X – 206400 = 247X + 104000

97X = 310400

X = 3200

Z = X \(\div\) 4Y

Z = 3200 \(\div\) 8

Z = 400
Hence, option C is correct.

Used Concepts:

  • Profit ratio = Capital × Time

  • Individual profit share = (Capital–time ÷ Total capital–time) × Total profit
